census_measured.babelmandeb_transiting_lanes_detail: All 8 are Djibouti local hops (sea_djibouti <-> sea_jeddah / sea_kingabdullahport / sea_portsudan / sea_salalah). The remaining 2 union lanes are incident legs ending at the strait (chk_babelmandeb->sea_jeddah, sea_colombo->chk_babelmandeb).
census_measured.suez_transit_completions_red_sea_window: In the baseline run, Suez-lane completions in the metric window are carried ~85% by corridor-membership lanes (rendered paths passing within the 100 km corridor of chk_suez); the through (Bab el-Mandeb) component is 0.

evidence.finding: The rendered path routes around the Cape of Good Hope (transit list: chk_capeofgoodhope, sea_portsaid) yet is tagged as Suez-transiting: its closest approach to chk_suez is 94 km at a shared canned waypoint (31.26, 32.3) that many lanes' polylines pass through. Its closest approach to chk_babelmandeb is 1,612 km — the polyline never enters the Red Sea.
Renders via Beirut and Port Said and picks up the same phantom Suez corridor tag at the shared waypoint; a Mediterranean local service counted as Suez-transiting.
Its Dijkstra path runs overland via Baku — the rendered path is a display composite, not a sea route; no Red Sea water is crossed.

No Suez-transiting lane's rendered path comes within 1,000 km of chk_babelmandeb (nearest: Red Sea port -> Port Said lanes, 1,022 km — they lie inside the Red Sea, north of the strait). No Bab el-Mandeb-transiting lane approaches Suez. The two corridors share no lane.

method: Derivation at the baseline Red Sea run's configuration (seed 42 from 2023-12-01, full graph as shipped, graph SHA-256 9743a288fb5d670d8f814f4f6240bab395fd72b7f63ee50475793539e564a062). Corridor membership = the sim's own transit identification (a lane transits a place when its rendered path's transit list includes it) unioned with incident lanes (a lane ending at the place). Through share measured two ways: lane count and simulated daily departures over the baseline Red Sea window.

observed_lane_structure_portwatch.reading: The two straits carry near-identical daily volumes: in reality essentially every Suez transit is also a Bab el-Mandeb transit (Asia-Europe services use both), so the real through share is ~100% of Suez traffic.
observed_lane_structure_portwatch.source: IMF PortWatch daily chokepoint series, stored in red_sea/actuals.json

question: Does the modelled lane census mis-weight through services — specifically Suez-transiting services that also transit Bab el-Mandeb — relative to the real lane structure PortWatch records?

verdict.census_weights: FAITHFUL — no mis-weighting found. The lane census counts the graph's legs with their modelled shares; there is no through-service entry to under- or over-weight, and no weight edit inside the census could manufacture one.
verdict.consequence_for_scorecard_v2: RS-3 (the exposed-subpopulation metric) resolves as registered: UNDEFINED — NO EXPOSED LANES IN CENSUS, excluded from aggregates, with the ungraded corridor decomposition printed beside it.
verdict.data_change: NONE. Any correction that moves the through share — surveyed route geometry, or explicit service patterns spanning legs — changes data/graph/graph.json, the shared graph contract pinned by SHA-256 in the causal-chain scorecard and other consumers, which is outside the scope of the sim layer (server/sim + sim data/census + data/sim_backtest). The correction is scoped here so a future graph revision can execute it: replace rendered-path corridor membership with surveyed per-lane water routes for the long-haul lanes, or add a service layer above legs carrying explicit transit sequences.
failure_located: (i) Transit identification runs over rendered paths, which are display composites (Dijkstra over the place network with canned waypoints), not surveyed sea routes: corridor membership by proximity to those polylines both invents Suez transits (Cape-routed and Mediterranean lanes tagged at a shared waypoint) and misses the real Red Sea passage entirely.

(ii) The census is a census of LEGS. End-to-end service patterns (a Colombo-Rotterdam service transiting Bem then Suez) do not exist as objects anywhere in the graph data, so no leg-level census can express the through share PortWatch observes.
